children: Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook said high inflation may require more rate increases, arguing that September’s single 1/4-point hike may not be enough to change inflation’s path. She made the remarks at the Central Bank of Chile’s annual conference in Santiago after dissenting at the Fed’s October meeting in favor of a quarter-point hike rather than a hold, according to BeInCrypto. Cook said financial conditions remained too loose, citing continued AI investment and stock prices supporting consumer spending, and warned that delayed action could require larger hikes later.

A tech-led stock selloff on Friday sent investors into Treasury bonds, while weak factory data added to market concerns. CME FedWatch showed the odds of no December hike rising from zero to about 11% in a day; its listed probabilities were 11.4% for a hold and 88.6% for a hike, while traders saw roughly even odds of a second hike by January. Bitcoin fell below $60,000 this week, reaching 2-year lows. October personal consumption expenditures inflation data is due November 25; Cook cited an estimate of 3.8%. A hotter reading could bolster her case for further hikes, while cooling inflation could strengthen bets on a pause at the December 8 and 9 meeting.

title: Lisa Cook Says Fed Rate Hikes Could Extend Beyond December
